intro: Whether you are purchasing your first home in Wichita, moving to Overland Park or exploring properties in Topeka, Lawrence or rural Kansas, knowing your expected monthly housing expenses can help you establish a realistic budget.

Our free Kansas mortgage calculator estimates your monthly payment based on your home price, down payment, interest rate and repayment period. Include property taxes, homeowners insurance, private mortgage insurance and association fees to compare financing options before committing to a property.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Kansas?

blocks.markdown:
A $220,000 Kansas home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,055.21.

This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or HOA fees. The interest rate, insurance premium and property taxes are illustrative rather than verified statewide averages.

Kansas offers housing opportunities across metropolitan areas, suburban neighborhoods, agricultural communities and smaller towns.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Kansas QuickFacts](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/KS/IPE120223), the median value of owner-occupied homes was $217,200 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Homeowners with mortgages reported median selected monthly ownership costs of $1,689, while approximately 67.2% of occupied housing units were owner-occupied.

These historical statistics provide useful context for understanding affordability but do not represent current property asking prices.

A home in Johnson County may have a different purchase price, property tax bill and transportation cost from a comparable property in western Kansas.

Before entering a purchase price into the calculator, research recent comparable sales within your preferred neighborhood.

sections.heading: How to Use the Kansas Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering the purchase price of the property you intend to buy.

Add your available down payment in dollars or as a percentage of the purchase price. A larger down payment reduces the amount you need to borrow.

Select your preferred mortgage term and enter the annual interest rate quoted by your lender.

Next, include the property's annual tax bill, homeowners insurance premiums and association fees where applicable.

Conventional borrowers making smaller down payments may also need private mortgage insurance.

Review the estimated monthly payment and use the amortization schedule to understand how your mortgage balance decreases over time.

Experiment with different purchase prices and financing terms before applying for a mortgage.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare financing scenarios outside Kansas.

sections.heading: How Kansas Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Kansas property taxes depend on appraised property values, statutory assessment ratios, local mill levies and applicable exemptions.

County appraisers determine property valuations, while local taxing authorities establish the rates used to calculate tax liabilities.

The [Kansas Department of Revenue's property tax calculation guide](https://ksrevenue.gov/propertyvaluation/ptbasics/slide03.html) explains the relationship between appraised value, assessed value and mill levies.

### Kansas residential property assessment ratio

Residential real estate generally uses a statewide assessment ratio of 11.5%.

This means a residential property appraised at $220,000 would have an assessed value of $25,300.

The assessment ratio is not the percentage of your home's market value that you pay annually in taxes.

Instead, the relevant mill levy is applied to this smaller assessed value.

### Kansas property tax calculation example

Suppose a home has an appraised value of $220,000 and an illustrative combined mill levy of 130 mills.

The actual tax bill may include exemptions, credits, special assessments and other adjustments.

Contact your county appraiser or county clerk to obtain the applicable valuation and levy rates.

### Kansas school finance levy exemption

Kansas provides an exemption on a specified portion of residential property value for the statewide school finance levy.

The [Kansas Department of Revenue's property tax exemption directory](https://www.ksrevenue.gov/pvdptexemptions.html) identifies the applicable statutory provision under K.S.A. 79-201x.

This exemption applies specifically to the statewide school finance portion of the tax bill. It does not automatically reduce every county, city or school district levy.

Confirm the applicable exemption amount for the relevant tax year rather than relying on older published examples.

### Kansas homestead property tax refunds

Certain homeowners may qualify for property tax relief through state refund programs.

The [Kansas Homestead Refund Programs directory](https://ksrevenue.gov/perstaxtypeshs.html) describes three arrangements:

- The Kansas Homestead Refund Program.
- Property Tax Relief for eligible low-income seniors.
- Property Tax Relief for qualifying seniors and disabled veterans.

Eligibility depends on income, residency, homeownership and other statutory conditions.

Because these programs generally involve refunds, do not automatically subtract an anticipated refund from your lender's monthly escrow payment.

Kansas homeowners should carefully evaluate insurance coverage because severe weather can affect both property maintenance expenses and insurance premiums.

The state experiences thunderstorms, tornadoes, hail and damaging winds. Flooding may also affect properties in certain locations.

Obtain property-specific insurance quotes before completing your mortgage application.

### Wind and hail insurance

Roof damage is an important consideration when comparing Kansas homeowners insurance policies.

Ask your insurer whether roof claims are settled using replacement cost or actual cash value.

Replacement cost coverage generally considers the expense of replacing damaged property with comparable materials, while actual cash value may account for depreciation.

Some policies also include separate wind and hail deductibles.

For example, a 2% deductible calculated against $250,000 of dwelling coverage would equal $5,000 for a covered claim to which that deductible applies.

Review the [Kansas Department of Insurance's homeowners insurance resources](https://www.insurance.kansas.gov/consumers/home-and-renters) before selecting coverage.

### Flood insurance in Kansas

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding.

The [Kansas Department of Insurance's storm and flood guidance](https://www.insurance.kansas.gov/consumers/storm-and-flood) provides additional information about coverage limitations and flood protection.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate your property's flood exposure.

Include separate flood insurance premiums in the mortgage calculator where applicable.
The following calculations assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These figures exclude property taxes, insurance, PMI and association fees.

Use the complete Kansas mortgage calculator to compare actual housing expenses associated with different properties.

The Kansas Housing Resources Corporation, commonly known as KHRC, administers homeownership assistance programs for eligible residents.

### Kansas First Time Homebuyer Program

The [Kansas Department of Commerce's housing resources](https://www.kansascommerce.gov/housing/) identify the First Time Homebuyer Program as a source of down payment and closing cost assistance.

The program targets qualifying lower-income households and provides assistance through a forgivable second mortgage.

Published 2026 program materials describe assistance ranging from 15% to 20% of the home's purchase price, subject to eligibility requirements.

Applicants generally need to meet household income, purchase price, occupancy and first-time buyer requirements.

The [KHRC homebuyer eligibility page](https://kshousingcorp.org/first-time-home-buyer-journey/) also specifies that participants generally contribute between 1% and 10% of the purchase price from their own funds.

### Location restrictions

The KHRC First Time Homebuyer Program does not operate in Johnson County or within the city limits of:

- Topeka.
- Lawrence.
- Wichita.
- Kansas City, Kansas.

These jurisdictions administer their own federal HOME funding and may provide separate assistance opportunities.

Buyers should investigate their local housing authority's programs before assuming KHRC assistance is available in their preferred location.

### Understanding forgivable financing

Forgivable assistance is different from an unconditional grant.

The KHRC assistance arrangement can be forgiven after ten years, subject to program requirements.

Selling or otherwise failing to satisfy applicable conditions before the forgiveness period ends may create repayment obligations.

Review the financing documents with your participating lender before incorporating assistance into your purchase budget.

Conventional financing may suit buyers who meet standard credit, income and down payment requirements.

FHA-insured mortgages offer another financing option for eligible households, although borrowers should account for applicable mortgage insurance premiums.

Eligible veterans, service members and surviving spouses may investigate [VA home loan programs](https://www.va.gov/housing-assistance/home-loans/), which may allow qualified borrowers to purchase without a down payment.

Buyers considering smaller Kansas communities can also explore [USDA Rural Development housing programs](https://www.rd.usda.gov/).

USDA financing depends on household income, property location and other lending requirements.

Compare the complete mortgage payment and upfront expenses associated with each program before making a financing decision.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Kansas Home

blocks.markdown:
Mortgage payments represent only one part of your homeownership budget.

Kansas homeowners should prepare for recurring maintenance, seasonal heating and cooling expenses, insurance deductibles and unexpected repairs.

Buyers considering older properties should inspect roofing, foundations, electrical systems and heating equipment before purchasing.

Rural properties may also require private well maintenance, septic system repairs or additional transportation expenses.

Newer developments can have special assessments associated with roads, utilities and other infrastructure improvements.

Request information about outstanding assessments and determine whether they appear on the property's existing tax bill. Avoid counting the same expense twice in your mortgage calculations.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Kansas?

blocks.markdown:
Start with your reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial obligations.

Include groceries, utilities, transportation, childcare, insurance premiums, debt payments and regular savings contributions.

Our [Kansas Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/kansas-paycheck-calculator/) can help you estimate income after payroll deductions, while our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) can help assess your existing borrowing obligations.

Maintain an [emergency fund](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) for repairs and insurance deductibles rather than using all your available savings for the down payment.

Compare multiple mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

A lender's maximum approved mortgage amount is not necessarily the amount that best fits your household budget.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $220,000 Kansas home?

With a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,055.21. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### How are Kansas residential property taxes calculated?

Kansas generally assesses residential property at 11.5% of its appraised market value. Applicable mill levies are then applied to the assessed value, with adjustments for eligible exemptions and other charges.

### Does Kansas offer down payment assistance for first-time buyers?

Yes. KHRC administers a First Time Homebuyer Program that provides qualifying households with down payment and closing cost assistance. Geographic restrictions, income limits, purchase price limits and forgiveness conditions apply.
